issues.failure_explanation: The displayed variation-of-constants formula does not satisfy iψ'+μψ=f: it has both the wrong exponential sign and the wrong forcing factor. In the uniqueness argument, (ψ',e^{-t/T}ψ') is real, so the real part of i(ψ',e^{-t/T}ψ') is zero, not the positive derivative norm written in the proof; moreover, the remaining μ-terms would not imply vanishing when μ<0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by the correct variation-of-constants expression and use it directly for both existence and uniqueness.
issues.overall_effect: The stated existence and uniqueness conclusion is true in principle but is not established by the proof as written.

issues.failure_explanation: Linearity applied to \eqref{eq:21} gives i q^{B^p}-ρq^{C^p}, not \eqref{eq:25}. More fundamentally, q^{B^p} is palindromic while q^{C^p} is anti-palindromic, so their nontrivial combination is generally not reciprocal under z↦1/z. Thus the asserted reciprocal root pairing and the resulting count of roots inside and outside the unit circle do not follow. The actual complex coefficients may support a self-inversive symmetry involving reciprocal conjugates, but that is a different argument.

failure_location.quote: In particular, from these expressions, both $q^{\B^p}$ and $q^{\bC^p}$ are reciprocal polynomials, and from \eqref{eq:25}, it follows that $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$ is also a reciprocal polynomial for all $\rho \in \R$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incorrect reciprocal-polynomial argument by a correct self-inversive or equivalent root-pairing analysis, and re-establish the required inside/outside root count.
issues.overall_effect: The root-distribution step needed to apply the Toeplitz conditioning theorem is unproved, undermining both stability theorems that rely on it.
issues.title: The symbol polynomial is not reciprocal as claimed

issues.failure_explanation: The Toeplitz analysis concerns a family indexed by n with ρ held fixed. For the original discretization with fixed physical parameter μ, however, ρ=μh varies with n and tends to zero. Pointwise algebraic conditioning for every fixed ρ does not provide uniform constants or exponents for the varying sequence ρ_n=μh_n, so it does not imply the advertised h-stability without a uniform-in-ρ estimate.

The theorem uses the converse implication: that weak conditioning of the Schur complement yields weak conditioning of the wave block matrix. That implication is not supplied by the lemma, and the proof gives no block-factorization estimates establishing it.
